## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Mahāassapura Sutta* ("The Longer Discourse at Assapura" or "The Greater Discourse at Assapura", MN 39) is the thirty-ninth discourse of the *Majjhimanikāya* [Ñāṇamoli & Bodhi 1995]. Set at the Angan town of Assapura, the Buddha addresses the mendicants to ensure they live up to the title and reputation of being recluses (*samaṇa*), exhorting them to practice in ways that fulfill the expectations of renunciants and cautioning them neither to exalt themselves nor disparage others [Goodwin 2012]. The text outlines the gradual training, laying down foundational mental and behavioral preliminaries—including moral shame and fear of wrongdoing, restraint of the sense faculties, mindfulness and clear awareness, and contentment—prior to meditation [Bodhi 2005; Kuan 2008].

Horner, and Bhikkhu Ñāṇamoli and Bhikkhu Bodhi, with Nyanaponika Thera providing a translation and study of the commentary on the sutta's similes [Ñāṇamoli & Bodhi 1995].

Full parallels to the discourse include Chinese versions in the *Madhyama Āgama* (MĀ 182) and *Ekottarika Āgama* (EĀ 49.8), as well as Sanskrit manuscript fragments (SHT sutta 9). Within the Pali Canon, its gradual training and meditation passages are closely shared with the *Sāmaññaphala Sutta* (DN 2), *Subha Sutta* (DN 10), and *Cūḷahatthipadopama Sutta* (MN 27) [Bodhi 2005]. DharmaNexus identifies thousands of matching characters across 173 Pali texts—most prominently with DN 10, AN 5, DN 2, and AN 4—and aligns the text cross-linguistically with MĀ 182, the Tibetan *Vinaya-kṣudraka-vastu*, the *Śrāvakabhūmi*, and Śāntideva's *Śikṣāsamuccaya* [DharmaNexus].
